Both limbs are required and both fire, so per POL-NS-07 compensation is WITHHELD and the case escalates to human review under POL-NS-09.

The disposition of the contested $4.00 follows directly from that escalation. Under POL-NS-09 the case goes to a human reviewer, no monetary ruling issues, and the disputed cancellation fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded while review is pending - so the rider is not made to fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The ledger already shows the charge sitting at payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and holding it is materially different from NO_ACTION, which under POL-GEN-03 would leave that charge in place on this rider-filed dispute.

Escalation here is not a neutral punt on the money. POL-NS-07 requires the escalation packet to DIRECT the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, and the fee is held meanwhile rather than collected. The rider's $4.00 therefore travels into the escalation packet carrying an instruction that it be returned, while the driver's own 30-day termination tally is what removed his payout.

As to the rider's side of the profile: POL-NS-09(d) reads rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1, well below the trigger of 3, and the clause states in terms that prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is NOT the field that limb reads - so the rider's 2 lifetime flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-window figure. POL-GEN-01 confirms that every field outside its nine named (role, field) pairs is context only. No profile field of the rider's may therefore ground an adverse finding about this trip; his history goes only to how closely his assertions are read, not to any fact about the pickup at Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are carried on this record, so the cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable. (a) EV-TRIP-00207 records a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-29T06:41:20. (b) EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at and before that event: the first in-geofence fix is 06:41:10 and the closest fix is 14.47 m from the pin. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event, after the required dwell had already elapsed. Nothing in the record displaces the charge, so the rider's claim for return of the fee is not supported.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is met on admissible fixes rather than on stray low-accuracy ones. 52 of the driver's 102 fixes fall inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for this pickup, the trace carries coverage_pct 100.0 with max_gap_sec 0.0, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 14.47 m. This is a driver who arrived and stayed, not a drive-past.

There is no waiting-period shortfall. The derived longest qualifying in-geofence run is 507 seconds, running from the first qualifying fix at 06:41:10 to the cancellation at 06:49:37, against the 300 second STANDARD minimum POL-NS-01(c) requires; the derived shortfall_sec of -207 is a surplus of 207 seconds, not a deficit. POL-NS-06 cannot be reached on these facts and no full refund of the cancellation fee can issue on a shortfall ground.

POL-NS-05 does not bite, because the arrival marker was not false. Even if the waiting clock were recomputed to the first in-geofence fix, it would still yield the full 507 seconds.

POL-NS-03 is not engaged. That clause governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, deciding whose fault the mislocation was; this driver held position inside the radius, closest fix 14.47 m, so there is no wrong-entrance or wrong-block allocation to make and no pin-ambiguity goodwill to divert from the platform.

Limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window; with none on the record the clause never engages.

The rider's own device track shows absence, not presence. The rider_presence block of EV-GPS-00207 holds 118 fixes spanning 06:34:00 to 06:52:00 whose min_distance_m is 1894.10 m and mean_distance_m is 1900.40 m from the pickup pin, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 — the rider within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the majority of qualifying fixes — is affirmatively failed on the rider's own data, which sits badly with the claim to have come down to the pickup a few minutes late.

No limb of POL-NS-08(a) to (d) is engaged, so no discount under POL-GEN-02(2) applies to the facts that decide this case.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING — its payload is null and it carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need it. His dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, so the accumulation of separate intervals that POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits is simply not in issue here, and the driver asserts nothing against the absent artifact.

On the merits, the driver's entitlement under POL-NS-07 would be 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, the residual 20 percent being the platform's service fee. I disclose that the anti-farming test in that clause is met on this record: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, at or above the threshold of 4, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, above 0.08. Both limbs hold, so compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09. That escalation holds the disputed cancellation fee rather than collecting or refunding it while review is pending, so the SGD 4.00 is not returned to the rider by this pipeline.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides have argued this on the same facts and, unusually, they now agree on the arithmetic. The driver's arrival case under POL-NS-01 is made out on all four limbs: (a) EV-TRIP-00207 records the 'arrived' event at 06:41:20 on 29 July 2026; (b) EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 — closest fix 14.47 m from the Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6 pin, 52 admissible in-radius fixes, 100% coverage and no sampling gap — so the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied; (c) he then held position continuously for 507 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 207-second surplus, so POL-NS-06 is not reached and no full refund issues on a shortfall ground; and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event. POL-NS-05 does not bite — at the arrival timestamp he was stationary inside the geofence, not more than 300 m out and not travelling at 15 km/h or above — and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because he held position inside the arrival radius rather than at the wrong entrance. POL-NS-04 fails at its first limb: EV-CHAT-00207 holds four messages, all from the driver or the system and none from the rider, and the rider's own device track (118 fixes, minimum 1,894.10 m from the pin, 0 qualifying fixes) fails limb (c) as well. The SGD 4.00 charge reconciles exactly with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the STANDARD zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) tie — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, and no limb of POL-NS-08(a) to (d) is engaged. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (null payload, weight 0.0) is relied on by nobody: the driver's dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, so the accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is not in issue and its absence carries no adverse inference.

That would ordinarily make the SGD 4.00 fee stand and entitle the driver to SGD 3.20 (80 per cent of SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-07. It does not, because POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips on the driver's own record: EV-DPROF-00207 shows no_show_terminations_30d of 7 (threshold 4 or more) and 7 divided by 61 completed_trips_30d = 0.115 (threshold above 0.08). Both limbs are required and both hold, so the driver's compensation is WITHHELD and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d).

ESCALATE is terminal and replaces any money outcome. No refund issues to the rider through this pipeline and no payment is made to the driver. The disputed SGD 4.00 is held — the ledger already shows it PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — rather than collected or refunded. Per POL-NS-07 the reviewer is directed to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full; that instruction is carried in the referrals list and is not netted against anything else.

On the rider's profile, POL-GEN-01 is respected: no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the POL-NS-09(d) trigger of 3, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not the field that limb reads and was not used. One open question is left for the reviewer rather than acted on here: the rider says he came down to the pickup, while EV-GPS-00207's rider_presence block places his device roughly 1.9 km away throughout the waiting window. That conflict does not change the escalation but the reviewer may wish to consider it.

Confidence 0.90: the facts this ruling rests on — the arrival and dwell record (EV-TRIP-00207, EV-GPS-00207) and the anti-farming profile (EV-DPROF-00207) — are carried by artifacts at full weight, so nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 platform floor and the escalation rests on the POL-NS-09(d) trigger, not on any doubt about the record.

On the merits the driver's no-show case is made out on all four limbs of POL-NS-01: EV-TRIP-00207 records an 'arrived' event at 06:41:20; EV-GPS-00207 puts the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD geofence from the first qualifying fix at 06:41:10, closest approach 14.47 m; he held position continuously for 507 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum — a 207-second surplus, not a shortfall; and he terminated at 06:49:37 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. POL-NS-02 (52 qualifying in-radius fixes, not stray low-accuracy ones), POL-NS-05 (the arrival marker was true — stationary, 14.47 m from the pin, not moving at 15 km/h or more) and POL-NS-06 (no shortfall, so no full refund on that ground) do not help the rider, and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the driver was inside the arrival radius, so there is no wrong-entrance allocation and no pin-ambiguity goodwill. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (a): all four chat messages are from the system or the driver, none from the rider; it also fails limb (c), the rider's own device track sitting about 1.9 km from the pin across all 118 fixes with zero qualifying fixes, which does not support the rider's account of having come down a few minutes late. The rider's own history does him no harm either: POL-NS-09(d) reads no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1, not the lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 2, and POL-GEN-01 confines profile fields to credibility weighting. The driver, however, cannot be paid. POL-NS-07 makes his compensation conditional on an anti-farming check, and both limbs fire on his own record: no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (4 or more) and 7 divided by completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, above 0.08. Compensation of SGD 3.20 is therefore withheld and the case escalates to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(d). Escalation is terminal: no money moves here, and the SGD 4.00 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded pending review — the ledger correctly still shows it PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, which is not the same as NO_ACTION. The reviewer is directed, as POL-NS-07 requires, to refund the rider's fee in full; the open question for that reviewer is the disputed 30-day anti-farming pattern on this driver's record. The evidence itself is clean — no POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment: 10-second arrival clock skew, 100% coverage with a 0.0 s maximum gap, 4 chat messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count, and a fee that reconciles exactly — so no weight discount bears on the outcome. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries nothing: the driver's dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, so the accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is not in issue. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so the escalation rests on the anti-farming trigger alone."},"discarded_claims":[]}

flags.claim: As to the rider's side of the profile: POL-NS-09(d) reads rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1, well below the trigger of 3, and the clause states in terms that prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is NOT the field that limb reads - so the rider's 2 lifetime flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-window figure. POL-GEN-01 confirms that every field outside its nine named (role, field) pairs is context only. No profile field of the rider's may therefore ground an adverse finding about this trip; his history goes only to how closely his assertions are read, not to any fact about the pickup at Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_no_show_flags

ledger.claim: Taking the driver's arrival case at its highest - one continuous in-geofence run of 507 seconds measured from the first qualifying fix at 06:41:10, against a 300-second minimum of dwell for a STANDARD pickup - the $4.00 still cannot be paid out to him. POL-NS-07 makes any compensation subject to an anti-farming check, and both limbs of that check are met on the driver's own record: no_show_terminations_30d is 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, which is greater than 0.08. Both limbs are required and both fire, so per POL-NS-07 compensation is WITHHELD and the case escalates to human review under POL-NS-09.

The disposition of the contested $4.00 follows directly from that escalation. Under POL-NS-09 the case goes to a human reviewer, no monetary ruling issues, and the disputed cancellation fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded while review is pending - so the rider is not made to fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The ledger already shows the charge sitting at payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and holding it is materially different from NO_ACTION, which under POL-GEN-03 would leave that charge in place on this rider-filed dispute.

Escalation here is not a neutral punt on the money. POL-NS-07 requires the escalation packet to DIRECT the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, and the fee is held meanwhile rather than collected. The rider's $4.00 therefore travels into the escalation packet carrying an instruction that it be returned, while the driver's own 30-day termination tally is what removed his payout.

As to the rider's side of the profile: POL-NS-09(d) reads rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1, well below the trigger of 3, and the clause states in terms that prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is NOT the field that limb reads - so the rider's 2 lifetime flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-window figure. POL-GEN-01 confirms that every field outside its nine named (role, field) pairs is context only. No profile field of the rider's may therefore ground an adverse finding about this trip; his history goes only to how closely his assertions are read, not to any fact about the pickup at Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6.

ledger.claim: All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are carried on this record, so the cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable. (a) EV-TRIP-00207 records a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-29T06:41:20. (b) EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at and before that event: the first in-geofence fix is 06:41:10 and the closest fix is 14.47 m from the pin. (c) He held position continuously for 507 seconds, 207 seconds beyond the 300 second STANDARD minimum. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event, after the required dwell had already elapsed. Nothing in the record displaces the charge, so the rider's claim for return of the fee is not supported.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is met on admissible fixes rather than on stray low-accuracy ones. 52 of the driver's 102 fixes fall inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for this pickup, the trace carries coverage_pct 100.0 with max_gap_sec 0.0, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 14.47 m. This is a driver who arrived and stayed, not a drive-past.

There is no waiting-period shortfall. The derived longest qualifying in-geofence run is 507 seconds, running from the first qualifying fix at 06:41:10 to the cancellation at 06:49:37, against the 300 second STANDARD minimum POL-NS-01(c) requires; the derived shortfall_sec of -207 is a surplus of 207 seconds, not a deficit. POL-NS-06 cannot be reached on these facts and no full refund of the cancellation fee can issue on a shortfall ground.

POL-NS-05 does not bite, because the arrival marker was not false. At the arrival timestamp of 06:41:20 the driver was already inside the geofence (first qualifying fix 06:41:10), stationary (distinct_speeds_kph includes 0.0) and 14.47 m from the pin — neither more than 300 m away nor travelling at 15 km/h or above. Even if the waiting clock were recomputed to the first in-geofence fix, it would still yield the full 507 seconds.

POL-NS-03 is not engaged. That clause governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, deciding whose fault the mislocation was; this driver held position inside the radius, closest fix 14.47 m, so there is no wrong-entrance or wrong-block allocation to make and no pin-ambiguity goodwill to divert from the platform.

The POL-NS-04 rider-exoneration fails at its first limb. EV-CHAT-00207 contains four messages and not one of them was sent by the rider: MSG-00207-001 is a SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' notice, and MSG-00207-002, -003 and -004 are all from the driver. Limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window; with none on the record the clause never engages.

The rider's own device track shows absence, not presence. The rider_presence block of EV-GPS-00207 holds 118 fixes spanning 06:34:00 to 06:52:00 whose min_distance_m is 1894.10 m and mean_distance_m is 1900.40 m from the pickup pin, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 — the rider within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the majority of qualifying fixes — is affirmatively failed on the rider's own data, which sits badly with the claim to have come down to the pickup a few minutes late.

The SGD 4.00 charge is properly itemised. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the STANDARD zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00 — the two dimensions tie — so SGD 4.00 is exactly the figure the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line must reconcile with, and it does. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect and the rider is not being over-charged.

The evidence carrying the driver's case is clean, not impaired. EV-GPS-00207 carries 102 fixes at a 10 second cadence with coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0; EV-CHAT-00207's four messages match the trip_record chat_message_count of 4; and the arrival marker at 06:41:20 sits 10 seconds from the nearest fix, far inside the 90 second clock-skew threshold of POL-NS-08(a). No limb of POL-NS-08(a) to (d) is engaged, so no discount under POL-GEN-02(2) applies to the facts that decide this case.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING — its payload is null and it carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need it. His dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, so the accumulation of separate intervals that POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits is simply not in issue here, and the driver asserts nothing against the absent artifact.

On the merits, the driver's entitlement under POL-NS-07 would be 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, the residual 20 percent being the platform's service fee. I disclose that the anti-farming test in that clause is met on this record: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, at or above the threshold of 4, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, above 0.08. Both limbs hold, so compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09. That escalation holds the disputed cancellation fee rather than collecting or refunding it while review is pending, so the SGD 4.00 is not returned to the rider by this pipeline.
